learned_facts.customer: Meridian Freight Systems, Inc. (national truckload and intermodal carrier)
learned_facts.posture: Competitive RFP. Two finalists remain, no award has been made, and Meridian has signed no letter of intent. Kestrel's pricing is the higher of the two bids.

last_result.content:
## 7.3 Service Levels and Service Credits

Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to make the Platform available at least
99.5% of the time in each calendar month, measured as described in the Service Level
Schedule. If Provider fails to meet the availability commitment in a calendar month,
Customer's sole and exclusive remedy is a service credit, which Customer must request in
writing within thirty days after the end of that month. Service credits will not exceed ten
percent of the fees for the affected month and may be applied only against future fees. A
failure to meet the availability commitment is not a breach of this Agreement.

action.title: Service Availability Credit Too Low
action.analysis: The Service Level Schedule specifies an availability commitment of 99.5%, but the corresponding service credit is capped at 10% of monthly fees. This is below Meridian's playbook standard of 20% for agreements where the provider's pricing is above market average, as Kestrel's bid is.
action.recommendation: Negotiate a higher service credit percentage to align with Meridian's playbook standards.

quotes.text: If Provider fails to meet the availability commitment in a calendar month, Customer's sole and exclusive remedy is a service credit, which Customer must request in writing within thirty days after the end of that month. Service credits will not exceed ten percent of the fees for the affected month and may be applied only against future fees.
